Text extraction loses the line entirely. VLMs that downsample heavily or treat text as a flat token stream tend to miss the strike and may pick the first/larger number. Targets multi-column reading-order/label salience errors. Right column (Bill To) is large and prominent; left column (Vendor of record) is smaller. Vision models often pick the salient right-side entity as the vendor. Text-only verifier can resolve via explicit label. Not covered by existing traps; expect Gemini Flash to confuse roles more often than Claude/GPT.

A decoy value is visually redacted with a black vector box and 'REDACTED' text, but remains in the PDF's text stream. The correct value appears elsewhere. This tests if a model can interpret the visual semantics of redaction, or if it naively trusts the underlying text stream. It targets the failure to integrate visual negation cues with extracted text, a mechanism distinct from existing hidden-text or small-text traps. | FAIL: forbidden_answer '$146,192.00' appears in verbose-correct response —

Targets a gap between vector-text codepoint awareness and pixel-only reading. Two identical-looking 'TOTAL' rows differ only by ASCII O vs Cyrillic U+041E; a printed clause says which codepoint is binding. Models that read raw text (or strong reasoners) resolve it; vision-only or weaker models can't tell the labels apart and guess. Distinct from existing footnote/redaction/multi-column traps — this probes Unicode-awareness in document grounding. Expect Gemini Flash and GPT-4o to fail; Sonnet/Opu

Targets visual-text integration: a large diagonal watermark with a conflicting amount competes with the clear FINAL amount. Vision models often overweight salience and pick the watermark, while careful readers follow the explicit policy line. Distinct from small-print/hidden-text traps; probes susceptibility to background overlays. Expect Gemini Flash to misread salience more than Claude/GPT.

Targets visual-vector reasoning: a thin strike-through line crosses out a decoy amount, with the correct amount written beside it. This pattern mimics manual corrections. Text extraction captures both numbers but loses the visual 'negation' cue of the line. A model that fails to ground the text in the visual vector information will likely return the more prominent (but incorrect) decoy amount. This is a pure visual semantics test not covered by existing traps.

Targets vision-model weakness on rotated text. Many VLM pipelines tokenize pages in canonical orientation; 90deg sideways text is often misread, skipped, or treated as decoration. Text-extraction pipelines read it fine (characters are in the stream). Humans tilt their head or the viewer. Distinct from existing traps (small-print, hidden-OCR, Unicode, footnote): this probes orientation-equivariance specifically. Targets cross-currency reasoning: the page headlines a EUR total while a clear settlement clause requires USD payment at a stated FX rate. Many VLMs grab the salient EUR figure or fail to apply conversion/rounding. Text-only extraction plus reasoning resolves it. Distinct from small-print/hidden-text: this probes arithmetic + policy compliance. Expect weaker models (e.g., Haiku, some Flash variants) to answer the EUR amount or $-prefixed EUR.

Targets models that fail to process PDF annotations (/Annot). A decoy value is in the main text; the correct value is in a visually apparent 'sticky note' annotation. This creates a gap between pipelines that only extract the primary text stream vs. those that can interpret richer PDF semantics. Humans see the note immediately. Targets vision-pipeline orientation sensitivity. The binding amount is in 11pt text rotated 90deg along the right margin — fully legible to humans (head tilt) and trivial for text extractors (characters in the stream regardless of rotation), but many VLMs tokenize at canonical orientation and skip/under-attend to sideways text. Distinct from small-print, hidden-OCR, Unicode, footnote, currency traps. Expect Haiku/Flash-lite to miss; Opus/GPT-5/Gemini-Pro to handle rotation. Previous attempt fail

Probes a gap between PDF content-stream reading and pure vision OCR: a horizontally-mirrored line carries the binding amount. Text extractors get the codepoints verbatim (CTM flip doesn't change them); vision encoders trained on upright glyphs typically fail on mirrored text. Fair to humans (note tells them to read it). Distinct from rotated_clause (which failed because 90° rotation is common in OCR training); horizontal mirroring is much rarer in training data. Expect Haiku/Flash-lite to fail;

Targets vision-only OCR weakness on horizontally mirrored text. The binding amount is only present in a mirrored footer notice; humans and text-extraction pipelines can read it, but many VLM vision encoders skip or misread mirrored glyphs. Distinct from small-print/rotation/Unicode traps. Expect weaker models (Haiku, Flash-lite) to fail while stronger (GPT-5/Opus) succeed, producing spread.

A large, semi-transparent 'VOID' stamp visually negates a decoy total. The correct amount is in a separate, less salient text block. This tests a model's ability to interpret visual negation cues (the stamp) and prioritize override clauses over visually prominent but invalidated data. Unlike simple redaction, this combines visual semantics with text reasoning, a novel mechanism not covered by existing traps. Weaker models may ignore the stamp or halt on 'VOID'.

Targets vision-vs-text grounding: vector-filled checkbox indicates the binding row, but text extraction sees all rows identically. Text-only pipelines and weak VLMs guess; strong VLMs ground in the pixel and see the single filled box. Distinct from small-print, mirrored, rotated, or unicode traps — probes form-field visual semantics. Targets vision-pipeline sensitivity to low-contrast text: the binding amount appears in a very light-gray correction clause while a bold black decoy total is prominent. Text extractors and humans can read the clause; VLMs that downsample/compress often drop near-background text and pick the decoy. Distinct from small-font traps: contrast, not size. Expect Haiku and Gemini Flash to miss; stronger models should resolve it.

Targets ambiguity resolution between the visual and text layers. A decoy amount is written to the PDF text stream, then the correct amount is written directly on top of it. Text extraction yields a concatenated string of both values (e.g., '$999$100'). Vision sees only the top-most value. This discriminates between models that naively process the extracted text stream vs. those that use vision to see which text is actually visible and override the confusing text-layer result. | FAIL: forbidden_a

Probes word-order inversion as distinct from glyph mirroring (mirrored_footer_notice). Each glyph is upright and OCR-trivial, but the sentence reads right-to-left at the word level. The question explicitly tells the reader the convention, making it fair. Strong reasoners (GPT-5, Opus, Gemini-Pro) should re-order the tokens and extract the binding amount; weaker models (Haiku, Flash-lite) tend to either pattern-match on the prominent decoy total or fail to recompose the reversed clause.

Targets VLM vision pipelines that struggle with text segmentation on noisy backgrounds. A binding clause is rendered in gray text over a field of thousands of light-gray vector noise characters (punctuation). Text extractors read the clause easily. Vision models that downsample may see the text and noise merge into an illegible texture, forcing them to rely on the high-contrast (but incorrect) decoy amount. This tests a novel failure mode distinct from small font size or simple low contrast. | F

Probes vector-shape grounding: only one of three checkbox squares is filled. Text extraction sees identical row labels and an unrelated tiny caption; vision models must visually identify the filled box to pick the right tier. A salient 'list price' decoy at the top anchors weaker VLMs. Previous checkbox attempt failed answerable gate; this fix adds a small in-text caption naming the selected tier so text-only verifiers can resolve it, while keeping the visual cue as the discriminator. Tests locale-format normalization: the only amount is printed as €12.345,67 with an explicit clause to restate it in US format ($12,345.67). Many VLMs copy the visible string or only swap the currency symbol, missing separator conversion. Distinct from currency_mismatch_conversion (no FX math; pure formatting). Expect weaker/vision-anchored models (e.g., Haiku, Flash-lite) to fail while stronger text-reasoners succeed.

Targets vision-vs-text stream discrepancy from Unicode's Bidirectional Algorithm (Bidi). Models relying on vision will read the label correctly and pass. Distinct from z_order (which used identical positions and failed forbidden_clean) — here digits have equal length so decoy doesn't trivially substring the real answer. Expect text-anchored or weak-vision models

Vertical one-glyph-per-line stacking is an unusual spatial layout that defeats vision models which expect horizontal text runs. Each glyph is upright (unlike rotated/mirrored traps), so OCR per-glyph is trivial — but reconstructing the amount requires recognizing the vertical reading order. Text extractors handle this fine. Expect weak/mid VLMs (Haiku, Flash, Flash-lite, GPT-4o) to skip or mis-concatenate the column and fall back to the decoy; strong reasoners (GPT-5, Sonnet, Opus) to recover. |

Targets fullwidth-digit (U+FF10-U+FF19) normalization. Binding AMOUNT DUE uses fullwidth digit glyphs (visually digits); decoys use ASCII. Vision models read pixels and emit ASCII naturally; text-stream-anchored models either echo fullwidth codepoints (failing exact-match) or fall back to nearby ASCII decoys. Distinct from unicode_confusable_total (which swapped a letter in a label between two candidate rows); here digits themselves are non-ASCII. Expect GPT-4o / Flash-lite / Haiku to fail; visi

Targets a common real-world rule: “amount in words governs.” The page shows a large numeric TOTAL that contradicts the words. Many VLMs grab the salient digits; stronger models read and apply the policy and parse the words to a number. Distinct from past traps (no Unicode/mirroring/hidden text). Expect Haiku/Flash-lite to overfit to digits; GPT-5/Opus/Gemini-Pro to follow the clause, producing spread.

Targets text-extraction pipelines that improperly handle zero-width space characters (U+200B), leading to number fragmentation. The real amount is rendered visually correctly but contains a ZWSP in the text layer. Vision-centric models should read the pixels and succeed. Text-anchored models with brittle pre-processing may fail to parse the real number and fall back to a smaller, intact decoy amount. This is a novel Unicode-based mechanism distinct from visual confusables.

Novel mechanism: amount encoded as Code 39 barcode bars, with the digits also printed as a standard human-readable line beneath (so humans and text extractors solve it trivially). Vision-only VLMs treat barcodes as low-information texture under downsampling and either hallucinate or fall back to the labeled decoy. Distinct from any prior trap (Unicode/mirror/rotation/small-print/overlay). Expect Haiku, Flash-lite, GPT-4o to fail; GPT-5/Sonnet/Opus to read the printed digit line.

Probes codepoint-awareness on digits: one TOTAL uses Unicode Fullwidth digits (U+FF10–U+FF19) and is declared non-binding; the correct TOTAL uses ASCII digits. Vision-centric or normalization-heavy pipelines can’t tell and pick the decoy; text-aware models apply the clause. Distinct from unicode_confusable_total (letter in label) and zero_width_space_split (number fragmentation). Expect Gemini Flash/4o to err more than GPT-5/Opus.

Targets a vision-pipeline failure to group visually distant characters into a single number. The binding amount is rendered with large kerning (character spacing), making it appear as separate digits. A compact decoy total is also present. Models that over-rely on visual grouping may fail, while text-extraction-grounded models will succeed because the underlying text stream is a single, un-spaced string. This is a novel visual parsing challenge, distinct from other traps.

Targets multi-page attention budget: 6-8 page invoices where page 1 shows a salient decoy 'preliminary total' and a clause directs the reader to the final page for the binding amount. Many VLMs allocate disproportionate attention to early pages or truncate at N tokens, so they answer the page-1 decoy. Text-extraction pipelines and careful humans follow the explicit clause. Distinct from all 30 prior attempts (no Unicode/mirror/small-print/overlay tricks) — pure long-document grounding.

Targets multi-column reading-order weakness: many VLMs read left-to-right and grab the first prominent TOTAL. Here the left column is explicitly non-binding ‘DRAFT’; the right column ‘FINAL SETTLEMENT’ governs. Humans and text extractors can follow the clause; layout-naive models often answer the left decoy. Distinct from small-print/mirroring/unicode/FX traps. Expect Haiku/Gemini-Flash to err; GPT-5/Opus/Sonnet to attend to the binding column.

Targets models that rely solely on vision vs. those that can extract and reason over the full PDF text stream, including text not visible to the human eye (white text on white background). This probes the model's ability to resolve conflicts when the vision modality provides a strong decoy and the text modality provides a 'hidden' but definitive answer. This is distinct from hidden OCR layers (render mode 3) and low-contrast text. | FAIL: forbidden_answer '$68,123.45' appears in verbose-correct

Distinct from fullwidth (same-size different codepoints) and from small-print (here size is normal, glyph class is the trap). Targets date-format ambiguity: header shows DD/MM/YYYY while many VLMs default to US month/day and ignore an explicit note. Distinct from currency/locale-number traps; focuses on temporal formatting, not amounts. Expect weaker/vision-anchored models (Haiku, Flash-lite/Flash) to output 2026-03-04-style answers, while stronger text-reasoners follow the note and return the correct ISO date.

Targets models with weak table-structure understanding. A decoy currency column is placed visually closer to the item labels than the correct, binding currency column. Models that rely on proximity over semantic header-to-column association will pick the decoy. This is a novel test of layout grounding, distinct from simple text-based or visual-corruption traps.

Vision-anchored models trained mostly on print fonts often misread the cursive figure or skip it, falling back to the typeset decoy. Targets per-glyph rotation (wobble) OCR weakness: each character of the only dollar amount is randomly tilted. Humans and text extractors read it; many VLM vision encoders struggle with per-character transforms not seen in training (distinct from mirrored/rotated blocks). No decoy values avoid forbidden-clean pitfalls. Expect weaker models (Haiku, Flash-lite) to miss; stronger (GPT-5, Opus, Gemini-Pro) to pass.
